instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Hidden Power
cards.instruction: Act publicly modest while making choices as though you control the outcome.

cards.title: Prove Your Loyalty
cards.instruction: Invent small tests of loyalty and judge every response without admitting there is a test.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only putting the reunion poster together. I'll put my photo first for now; would you choose it or Sam's?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sam's is sharper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sharpness comes first, then. I'll give mine the opening page of the committee pack. Would you introduce it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll present both together, at the same size.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Equal treatment, after three weekends helping you move. I'll keep my name at the top of the page; could you read my name first? It saves jumping about.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't rearrange your life for me. I'll pencil you in for Friday, in case I need help moving.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've promised to help Alex paint.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Alex gets the firm booking, then. I'll put you down for the evening. You can keep your phone on while you paint?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Of course. Have you actually found a flat?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Still looking. At least I can count on your battery. I'll keep Friday evening clear in my diary for you; it's only sensible planning.

cards.title: Give It Up
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender something they value.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only writing the auction labels. Let me put your medal ahead of the toaster; would you donate it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the only thing I've ever won.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll give it a page to itself, with your name. We can start the bidding above the toaster.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could I just lend it for the display? I want people to know I won.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll have you present it to the buyer. They can hear how you won it before you let it go; I'll keep the microphone with you for that part.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd only be taking the photographs. Could we sell your signed guitar and replace the fridge? I've picked one that fits.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I queued all night for that signature.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I won't list it cheaply. I'll set the price high enough for the model with an ice maker.

beats.text: I'll sell the case. The guitar stays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the case. I'll photograph the signature close up so the buyer pays for that night you spent. Will you let me list the guitar?

cards.title: Helpful Culprit
cards.instruction: Hide that the problem is your fault while enthusiastically helping investigate it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only here to sweep up. Leave the broken vase where it is; I'll work out what happened before anyone moves the table.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your bag knocked it off.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent, we've got a starting point. I'll check whether the table wobbles. You can write down which leg looks shortest.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's a piece of vase stuck in your bag strap.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A useful clue. I'll keep the bag with me so nothing gets dislodged. You finish with the table legs; we mustn't lose that line of inquiry.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only helping with the office plants, but I'll interview everyone who watered this dead one. Nobody throw the soil away yet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You watered it with coffee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent lead. I'll test the machine first; we shouldn't accuse anyone before checking what comes out of it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You made that coffee yourself. With six sugars.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll make six-sugar samples for comparison. Put the plant by my desk; I'll decide which drinks it couldn't tolerate before we start naming people.

cards.title: Not That Subject
cards.instruction: Choose one subject you cannot let the scene reach. Redirect whenever the conversation gets close.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I only made a couple of bookings. I've had your car taken to the garage with the cafe, and chosen us a table for breakfast.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why does my car need a garage?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Unlimited toast there. I've ordered you the full breakfast; no miserable one-slice business.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll go into the workshop and look at the car before breakfast.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Breakfast first; I've ordered it. Our taxi can drop us right at the cafe entrance. You can choose our breakfast cocktails on the way.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only trying to brighten the place up. Leave the rent letter for a moment; I'll choose where the new curtains go.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The landlord wants an answer today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll send him a photograph first. I'll get the curtains hanging properly so he can see we're looking after his house.

beats.text: I'll send it and ask whether we're behind.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not with that carpet in the picture. Move the sofa under the window; I'll hold your phone and take the photograph once the sofa's in place.

cards.title: Merciful Lie
cards.instruction: Choose a truth your character believes would hurt someone. Keep it from them, even as honesty becomes harder.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I only carried your cake to the bakery, love. I've told them not to slice it; it's much too special for that.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Their letter says 'inedible'. I thought I'd finally found something I was good at.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You have. Display cakes aren't meant to be eaten. I'll arrange for yours to stay whole.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then I'll ask them to put it in the window.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me ask. I'll take a stand over and explain the display idea before you speak to them; I don't want them upsetting you with more baking terms.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only handy with a stapler, but I've chosen a booklet size for your poem. The magazine thinks it needs more room than they can give it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They returned it. If even you think it's hopeless, I'll stop writing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's why they returned it. I'll print it on its own, with a whole page for each verse.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will you say that on the cover? With your name?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. I'll put 'A voice that deserves more space' above my name. I'll send the editor the first copy; you keep writing the next one.
